construction: 69 parts in 1 step. A core of 2×6 bricks, 2×4/2×2 plates and 2×2 plates with holes carries two 30414 1×4 side-stud bricks; two 43712 6×4 triple-curved wedges and two 48183 3×4 wings sit on those side studs and on 3794a jumper plates. Two 42023 inverted curved slopes close the underside, two 61678 curved slopes and eight 54200 cheese slopes shape the top, a 3039pce printed radar slope is the instrument panel at the rear, and a 6233 cone with a 3942c cone ride a 32073 axle through a 32064b Technic brick.
interfaces: Stud directions: 69 parts, 51 up, the wedges facing ±Z, the cones facing −X. The rear plate layer and the Technic brick are the interfaces to the fuselage; the instrument slope faces the canopy.
lesson: A jet nose that tapers in two directions: the top with 4×1 curved slopes and 1×1 cheese slopes, the sides with 6×4 triple-curved wedges hung sideways on 1×4 side-stud bricks and jumper plates, and a 3×3 cone plus a 2×2 cone on a 5-long axle as the spike.
parent_context: `5892 - Airplane.ldr` places it at (−490, −32, 0) with the identity matrix: the nose points −X, ahead of the canopy and above the retracting nose gear.
reuse_notes: Use the pattern for any pointed nose: build a studs-up core one stud narrower than the fuselage, hang the curved side panels on side studs, and let a cone pair on an axle make the tip. Change the wedge part to change the curvature.
